question: What is the main goal of a two-way referral system in mental health care?

options.A: To permanently transfer all chronic clients to tertiary psychiatric hospitals
options.B: To reduce the total number of medications prescribed at primary clinics
options.C: To ensure smooth movement of clients and feedback between different levels of care
options.D: To allow primary nurses to independently diagnose complex psychiatric disorders

explanation: Think of a two-way referral as a team effort between clinics and big hospitals. It keeps communication flowing both ways so no patient is left stranded in the system! [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is downward referral just as important as upward referral in psychiatry?

options.A: It brings stable clients closer to home for routine maintenance and family support
options.B: It allows tertiary hospitals to avoid seeing clients with mild anxiety
options.C: It frees up bed space by permanently discharging clients from all medical follow-up
options.D: It punishes clients who refuse to take their psychiatric medications

explanation: Once a patient is stable, sending them 'downward' to a local clinic means they get check-ups right near their family without traveling far. That's a win for recovery! [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which facility represents the primary level of mental health care in Nigeria?

options.B: Local government health clinics and posts

explanation: Primary care is right at the grassroots level—the local health posts and clinics closest to our communities. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is a major consequence when clients bypass primary facilities to visit tertiary psychiatric hospitals directly?

options.A: Severe overcrowding and longer waiting times at tertiary centers
options.B: Faster recovery times for clients with mild anxiety
options.C: Better funding and resources for primary health clinics
options.D: Elimination of the need for a referral letter

explanation: When everyone goes straight to the big teaching hospitals for minor issues, those specialist centers get overwhelmed. That's why starting at the local clinic matters! [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: When should a primary health nurse initiate an upward referral for a psychiatric client?

options.A: As soon as the client's symptoms begin to improve on standard medication
options.B: Whenever the client misses a single routine clinic appointment
options.C: When the client develops severe psychosis or active suicidal ideation beyond local management
options.D: When the local clinic runs out of printed health education leaflets

explanation: If a patient's condition becomes too severe for the local clinic to safely handle—like active suicidal thoughts—it's time for an upward referral to specialists. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is an essential component of any upward referral from a nurse?

options.A: Cash payment for the specialist consultation at the tertiary gate
options.B: A clear clinical summary letter detailing history and current medications
options.C: A personal guarantee that the client will be admitted as an inpatient
options.D: Official approval from the local government chairman

explanation: Always send a proper handover note! A clear clinical summary helps the specialist know what you've tried and what the patient needs next. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a downward referral in mental health?

options.A: To clear hospital beds by discharging clients without any follow-up plan
options.B: To transfer chronic cases to out-of-state traditional healing homes
options.C: To return stabilized clients to community clinics for ongoing maintenance care
options.D: To punish clients who refuse to take part in group therapy sessions

explanation: Downward referral steps patients down to community care once they are stable, freeing up specialist beds while keeping them supported close to home. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: A client with schizophrenia is stable and ready for discharge from a tertiary psychiatric hospital. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Keep the client admitted for another year to prevent any possibility of relapse
options.B: Advise the client to stop taking medications since their mood is now normal
options.C: Prepare a discharge summary and link the client to their local primary health clinic
options.D: Send the client home without informing local clinic staff

explanation: Great nursing care means bridging the gap! Writing a good summary and linking the patient to their local clinic ensures they won't default on their meds. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which task is a key responsibility of the psychiatric nurse during a referral?

options.A: Diagnosing complex neurological disorders without a doctor
options.B: Buying the client's prescription drugs using personal funds
options.C: Making the final decision on hospital budgetary allocations
options.D: Providing education and preparing documentation for the client and family

explanation: Nurses play a vital role by calming fears, educating the family, and getting all the paperwork ready for a smooth transition. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is nurse-to-nurse communication important when transferring a psychiatric client?

options.A: It guarantees that the client will receive free hospital care
options.B: It replaces the need for any written medical diagnosis
options.C: It prevents family members from asking questions about the illness
options.D: It ensures vital behavioral observations and safety precautions are not missed

explanation: A verbal nurse-to-nurse chat shares crucial safety tips and behavioral clues that you won't always find written on a chart. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to mental health referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: High cost of transportation and out-of-pocket treatment expenses
options.B: Poor communication and missing feedback letters between facilities
options.C: Stigma and initial reliance on traditional or spiritual healers
options.D: Immediate availability of fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village

explanation: Spot the trick! Fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village definitely do not exist, making this option the false statement—and thus the correct answer. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: How does cultural stigma affect the two-way referral process?

options.A: It ensures that primary health clinics receive adequate funding from local chiefs
options.B: It delays initial professional help-seeking, often bringing clients to the hospital only in severe crises
options.C: It makes downward referral unnecessary because clients recover faster at home
options.D: It encourages families to maintain smooth communication with tertiary psychiatrists

explanation: Because of stigma, families often try other options first. By the time they reach the hospital, the illness has usually progressed to a crisis. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the benefit of using standardized referral proformas in mental health care?

options.A: They ensure that all essential clinical and historical data is consistently recorded
options.B: They automatically guarantee financial sponsorship for the client
options.C: They eliminate the need for nurses to speak with clients or families
options.D: They prevent tertiary hospitals from ever discharging clients back home

explanation: Using standard referral forms makes sure no important medical or social history gets accidentally left out. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why is receiving feedback from a tertiary center important for a primary care nurse?

options.A: It allows the primary nurse to take over the role of a specialist doctor
options.B: It reduces the workload at the local clinic to zero
options.C: It builds professional confidence and improves ongoing management of the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever needing medication refills again

explanation: Getting feedback closes the loop! It helps primary nurses learn from specialist outcomes and grow more confident in managing similar cases. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h7)
